title: Core Triage
eyebrow: Triage · house-rules core and the restructure into sub-plugins

short.lead: I sorted the 147 open issues that belong to the house-rules core or to the restructure into a core plus six sub-plugins (issue #306). Each one has a recommended category and triage state, and a target part taken from the restructure's systems document. The other 22 open issues are art pipeline, eldritch goose, Unity or Focus Deck work and were left out. Nothing has been labelled or closed yet. The full table, with what I checked in the code for each row, is docs/plans/2026-10-17-triage-core-restructure.md.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what it covers.
items: Clear specs with no open question, such as the attribution gaps in #315 "the attribution guard misses gh api and curl" and #191 "pull requests from a cloud session still credit Claude". Most are built inside their sub-plugin during the restructure, not in today's hook.py.

36 are built and labelled needs review, waiting for your testing. 19 more are probably fixed by that work, such as the prompt-timer issues that #290 "each prompt waits on its own" rebuilt; your testing settles them. The other 19 need a judgment call or another repo, such as #181 "report old claude/ branches across aj's repos".
Test or decide, at your own pace.

5 are the first rebuild plan (#208 to #212), which #306 replaced. 7 are already built or no longer apply, such as #178 "the attribution guard also checks GitHub tool calls", built at hook.py:6050. 11 are the old issue workflow, which #301 "other work becomes an issue in its own repo" replaces.
#45 "the vocabulary has nowhere to live", #140 "a handoff document at 95% usage" and #150 "follow a builder's progress from the phone" each leave an open question.
#215 and #229 describe the same verify.py temp-file failure. #193 and #260 both ask for permission prompts in plain words. One of each pair should close.
Closing #229 and #193 is part of the first choice under Choices.

changes: Each gets one category label (bug or Feature) and one triage state label.
No triage labels. Many issues carry several category labels and no state.
One category and one state each, as the table recommends. The existing labels "in progress" and "needs review" are left as they are.
Applied with the GitHub command-line tool (gh), one issue at a time, after your approval.
A comment on each saying what is settled and the specific question still open.
A comment that opens with a note saying an AI did the triage, then states the open question.
Only if you answer A to the choice about posting triage notes.
